scenes.title: Packing La Poderosa
scenes.caption: Before leaving Buenos Aires, Ernesto and Alberto had to fit their belongings onto one old Norton. The luggage left little room for its two riders.

scenes.title: A pause by the Atlantic
scenes.caption: In Miramar, Ernesto visited Chichina before continuing south. The seaside stop kept him close to home for a little longer.

scenes.title: Across the pampas
scenes.caption: Beyond Bahía Blanca, open country replaced the coast. Long unpaved roads made dust, luggage and the condition of the bike part of each day's travel.

scenes.title: The lakes at Bariloche
scenes.caption: At Bariloche, the journey reached Nahuel Huapí. Forested shores and mountain ridges offered a different view from the plains they had crossed.

scenes.title: Across the lakes into Chile
scenes.caption: The border crossing involved boats as well as roads. From the deck, the travelers could watch the wooded slopes rise steeply from the water.

scenes.title: News in Temuco
scenes.caption: A newspaper in Temuco reported their visit. The attention helped turn two travelers with an unreliable motorcycle into welcomed guests.

scenes.title: The motorcycle becomes cargo
scenes.caption: At Los Ángeles, they found a truck to carry them and the broken motorcycle to Santiago. La Poderosa would no longer carry them north.

scenes.title: What the road wore out
scenes.caption: A worn tire, a handful of tools and patched luggage tell another part of the trip. Keeping an old motorcycle moving required attention that no itinerary could predict.

scenes.title: Houses above the port
scenes.caption: Valparaíso rose in layers above its harbor. Its steep streets and crowded slopes belonged to a port where the next stage of their journey depended on finding a ship.

scenes.title: Working their passage
scenes.caption: After hiding aboard a coastal ship, the two men were put to work. Near Antofagasta, the desert coast came into view from the deck.

scenes.title: A night with fellow travelers
scenes.caption: On the way to the copper mine, they met a worker and his wife looking for employment. In the cold desert, they shared what little warmth they had.

scenes.title: The scale of Chuquicamata
scenes.caption: At Chuquicamata, the open pit cut into the desert in immense steps. The mine's scale set machinery and workers against a landscape being steadily removed.

scenes.title: Two histories in one street
scenes.caption: In Cusco, closely fitted Inca masonry survived beneath later buildings. Walking its streets meant seeing different periods of the city in the same wall.

scenes.title: Looking closely at the stonework
scenes.caption: A close view reveals how unevenly shaped blocks meet without wide mortar joints. These surviving walls gave the travelers something more concrete than a textbook account of the Inca city.

scenes.title: Machu Picchu above the valley
scenes.caption: At Machu Picchu, terraces and roofless stone buildings followed the mountain ridge. The site placed the remains of an Inca settlement within a much larger landscape.

scenes.title: Steps through the terraces
scenes.caption: From within the terraces, the view becomes smaller: retaining walls, narrow steps and planted ground. The stonework had to hold soil on a steep mountainside.

scenes.title: Evenings with Dr. Pesce
scenes.caption: In Lima, Dr. Hugo Pesce welcomed the travelers and helped them find lodging. Their visits brought medicine and conversation into the same evenings.

scenes.title: Lima's wooden balconies
scenes.caption: In the old center of Lima, enclosed wooden balconies projected above the street. The capital offered another layer of architecture after the stonework of Cusco.

scenes.title: At the river landing
scenes.caption: At Pucallpa, road travel gave way to river travel. A landing crowded with timber boats, sacks and passengers would have made the change of pace visible.

scenes.title: A berth on the riverboat
scenes.caption: On the riverboat, a hammock could serve as a berth. The shaded passenger deck put sleeping, luggage and conversation close together.

scenes.title: The river fills the view
scenes.caption: Near Iquitos, the river opened into broad reaches bordered by forest. From a low boat, the far bank could become a thin line across the water.

scenes.title: Time at San Pablo
scenes.caption: At San Pablo, they spent time with people receiving treatment for leprosy. Conversation and company formed part of the visit alongside their medical interests.

scenes.title: Turning twenty-four
scenes.caption: Ernesto turned twenty-four at San Pablo. At a birthday gathering, he thanked his hosts and spoke of Latin American unity.

scenes.title: Downstream on Mambo-Tango
scenes.caption: The next vessel was a raft called Mambo-Tango. Close to the water, shelter and supplies had to share a small floating platform.

scenes.title: A cold capital after the Amazon
scenes.caption: They flew from Leticia to Bogotá. The highland capital brought cool streets and tiled roofs after weeks among riverboats and tropical forests.

scenes.title: Separate plans in Caracas
scenes.caption: In Caracas, Alberto stayed while Ernesto prepared to return to Argentina. The shared journey ended with different plans for what came next.
